subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps for Acme - cost/latency/quality tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@acme.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps for Acme - cost/latency/quality tradeoffs

Hi Jordan / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great conversation; I left with a clearer sense of your priorities:
- Primary: fast low-latency responses for customer-facing summarization (SLO ~ <150ms 95th).
- Secondary: lower inference cost for nightly batch jobs (high throughput, tolerance for slightly higher latency).
- Must-have: model behavior consistency (few regressions) and ability to pin versions.

As promised, attached is a concise recommended model shortlist with rationale and a quick mapping to the evals we ran against your prompt set. High-level summary below — full details are in the spreadsheet and the benchmark PDF.

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality):
1) Llama2-Chat-70B-q4_0: Best-quality baseline for the hardest summarization cases. Highest token-quality but ~3-4x the latency/cost of smaller quantized variants. Good for canary/critical flows.
2) RedWood-7B-StreamQuant: Sweet spot for live UI — sub-150ms median on our Dedicated N10 GPUs, very low cost. Slightly lower factuality on very long context; we saw 92% pass on your regression prompt set.
3) Mistral-7B-v2-q4: Strong open model alternative with good latency and competitive cost. Slightly better factuality than some 7B quantized variants on your prompts, but larger memory footprint in multi-session scenarios.

Suggested rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Route 10% of live traffic to RedWood-7B-StreamQuant, 90% to your current model. Monitor regression metrics (we've pre-populated a small prompt set in the Drive link).
- Phase 2 (expand): If pass rate >95% on canary, migrate critical paths to 7B stream-quant. Keep Llama2-Chat-70B as fallback for high-risk cases.
- Batch jobs: Use Mistral-7B-v2-q4 for nightly batch to reduce cost; tune batch size for throughput.

Next steps I can take:
- Share a short mutual-action plan (MAP) with milestones and estimated cost delta across choices.
- Spin up a 48-hour dedicated canary on RedWood-7B-StreamQuant for your team to test.
- Add Rishi to a technical deep-dive on kernel/quant options next week.

Attachments: acme-model-shortlist.xlsx (shortlist + cost model), acme-prompt-set-v1.json (anonymized prompt set used for evals), redwood-benchmarks-acme-20260720.pdf (detailed latency/cost/quality charts).

Would love to align on which path you want to try first. If you're good, I'll draft the MAP and book the canary.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the ping Marissa — quick technical notes for the MAP/canary:

Canary config (proposed):
- Model: RedWood-7B-StreamQuant on Dedicated N10 (pinned version v2026-07-15).
- Traffic split: 10% live, 90% baseline.
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency target 150ms; monitor 50/95/99 percentiles.
- Observability: Enable request-level traces, tokenized cost logs, and KV-cache hit metrics. We'll export audit logs to your S3 bucket and enable 12-month retention.
- Regression detection: We pushed your anonymized prompt set to an eval job (see Drive link). Configure automated alerts for >3 regressions in a rolling 24h window.

Model tradeoff notes:
- Llama2-Chat-70B-q4_0: Use as guarded fallback. High-quality but cost ~3\u20134x of StreamQuant on same infra; also requires larger memory, so fewer concurrent sessions per GPU.
- RedWood-7B-StreamQuant: Engineered for low-latency streaming; quant kernels tuned for N10. Expected median ~80\u2013120ms, 95th ~140\u2013160ms depending on prompt lengths. Cost-efficient for interactive use.
- Mistral-7B-v2-q4: Best batch cost / throughput; consider for nightly summarization jobs where per-job latency is not critical.

Action items I can own:
- Provision a 48-hour canary environment (no charge) and a short runbook for procurement/compliance to review.
- Populate the MAP with concrete numbers for cost/capacity and share by EOD PT.

I'll attach a short canary runbook to the Drive link and include the precise kernel/quant flags we'll use.

Rishi Malhotra
Infrastructure Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
